text: Let's start with a cheap, interpretable baseline for 30-day readmission from the MIMIC-IV discharge notes: TF-IDF 1-3-grams + logistic regression, 5-fold CV, before trying anything heavier. Prior work reports 0.70-0.78 AUROC for bag-of-words baselines, so we expect AUROC >= 0.75.

text: The baseline reaches AUROC 0.54 (5-fold CV), barely above chance; the first attempt ran out of memory with max_features=None. The top-weighted features are note boilerplate ('patient was discharged home'), and negated findings ('no evidence of CHF') map to the same n-grams as positive ones.

Switch from sparse n-grams to frozen PubMedBERT embeddings instead. N-grams lose the clinical semantics we need: negations collapse into the same features as positives. Contextual embeddings handle negation and abbreviations, and we keep the encoder frozen so it fits the Colab T4 memory budget that the out-of-memory crash exposed.

title: Caveat: only one seed and one hospital so far
detail: Before claiming robustness we need >= 3 seeds with confidence intervals. No external validation: all notes come from a single hospital system (MIMIC-IV / BIDMC).
